issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double) while the concrete classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int). This parameter-type mismatch between the interface and its implementations (and the UML) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.raisePressure parameter type consistent with the UML and implementations. Change the Pneumatic interface method signature to void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (or alternatively update the UML and all implementations to use double). Ensure the interface and all implementing classes use the same parameter type so code compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int): void, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease). The concrete classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int), so the interface parameter type in the solution does not match the UML nor the implementations, causing a semantic/signature mismatch that will confuse students and break the mapping from the specification to the code (and will lead to compilation/test failures).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic interface signature with the UML and implementations by changing raisePressure's parameter type to int (i.e., void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease)); update the template and any implementations accordingly so the interface and concrete classes match the specification.
